proposal.title: First AWS sketch: agent-assist for synthetic support calls
proposal.body: Scope: consent check, audio ingestion, streaming transcription, PII redaction, grounded suggestions, agent-approved summary and CRM draft. Assumptions: synthetic audio only. The existing CRM is never written automatically; the agent submits approved drafts manually. Region, account, model ID and Bedrock access are not selected or verified. Most components are design only and outside current native generator coverage.

data.label: Support agent
data.description: Person handling the synthetic call; reviews suggestions and approves the summary and CRM draft.

data.label: Synthetic call audio
data.description: Pre-recorded synthetic caller/agent audio played as a stream. No real calls are placed.

data.label: Agent assist web app
data.description: Agent desktop showing the live redacted transcript and suggestions with sources. It records consent, summary approval and CRM draft approval.

data.label: Agent sign-in
data.description: Agent authentication with MFA; issues the tokens the API checks.

data.label: Assist API
data.description: Authenticated WebSocket/HTTP API for consent, suggestions and approvals. Uses a JWT authorizer; no anonymous access.

data.label: Consent gate
data.description: Blocks audio processing until consent is recorded for the call ID, and stops processing if consent is withdrawn.

data.label: Audio ingestion
data.description: Receives the call audio stream once consent is recorded.

data.label: Transcription
data.description: Streaming speech-to-text with speaker labels; returns transcript segments to the orchestrator.

data.label: PII redaction
data.description: Detects and masks personal information in each segment before storage or any model call.

data.label: Assist orchestrator
data.description: Receives redacted segments, retrieves knowledge, calls the model through guardrails, and returns cited suggestions, a draft summary and a CRM draft. It has no CRM write permission.

data.label: Support knowledge base
data.description: Approved support articles used for grounding. Source content is treated as untrusted data, and every suggestion cites its articles.

data.label: Output guardrails
data.description: Filters prompts and outputs (PII, denied topics, grounding check) around model calls.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Direct foundation model, not yet selected. Model access, region and quotas are unverified; mocked locally with scripted replies.

data.label: Call session and audit store
data.description: Stores consent records, redacted transcript, suggestions, the approved summary, the CRM draft and the approval audit trail, keyed by call ID with idempotent writes.

data.label: Monitoring
data.description: Logs, metrics and alarms for latency, errors and redaction failures. Logs contain no unredacted content.

data.label: Existing CRM
data.description: Existing CRM, outside the provisioning scope. The agent submits the approved draft manually; the system never writes to it.

edges.label: cited suggestions, summary and CRM drafts

requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: no audio may be ingested, transcribed or stored for a call until consent is recorded. Processing stops if consent is withdrawn.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Unredacted personal information could leak to model prompts or logs.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: personal information must be redacted from transcripts before storage, logging or any model call.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Automatic writes could corrupt customer records with unreviewed AI output.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Do not place calls or write CRM records automatically."
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the system must never place calls or write CRM records; the agent approves the summary and submits the CRM draft manually, and each approval is audited.

response.message:
The good news is that the check found no failures, and every component and connection is still in place. It stopped at 8 blockers because there's no supported generator for this kind of workflow yet. Those blockers fall into two groups:

- **Consent, audio streaming, transcription, sign-in, the API and the web app:** each needs real product work, meaning a native generator plus app code, before it can be tested. I can't fix this by changing the diagram. Swapping in the existing RAG web app, sign-in or API patterns would change what you asked for, and the consent and transcription steps have no supported pattern at all. So I haven't suggested any diagram changes. The steps to reproduce this are design revision 2 and artifact edcba137…, and the next run must use a new artifact.
- **The support agent and the synthetic call audio:** these are systems you already have, and each just needs a note saying where it comes from and who owns it. For the agent, that's the person using a browser, which the diagram already shows. The audio isn't described yet.

This was only a local check with scripted model replies, so it says nothing about transcription accuracy, how well personal details are hidden, or model quality. Nothing has been deployed, and no region or account access has been checked.

**Where does the synthetic call audio come from today?** For example, a set of recordings your team already keeps somewhere, or test files we'd create and look after as part of this project. Your answer settles how we describe that audio source and who owns it.
